recipeStatus: 0.1.0-draft — DemandBlue (Salesforce practice) channel recipes mapped from the marketing team's real asset vocabulary (email nurture TPs, SM posts, ISR scripts, CSS, one-pagers); pending DemandBlue Marketing Lead sign-off

recipes.label: LinkedIn / social posts (company + executive)
recipes.recipe: Feed-native posts. Company variants open with a feed-native hook and carry the campaign hashtag; executive variants are first-person POV, deliberately less corporate. Short paragraphs, no link dumps. Salesforce product names written exactly as Salesforce names them.

recipes.label: Email nurture touchpoints (TP sequence)
recipes.recipe: Each variant is one touchpoint in a multi-touch nurture sequence (the DemandBlue plan runs up to TP11). Subject-line-ready opening, one idea per touchpoint, a single low-pressure CTA. Sequence the variants so each moves the reader one step: problem awareness first, proof and customer evidence mid-sequence, decision-stage CTA last. Personal, one-to-one voice.

recipes.label: Sales battle card extract
recipes.recipe: Objection-ready summaries for ISR/Sales: objection, response grounded in a sourced claim, proof reference. Comparisons stay factual and sourced — never disparage competitors. Internal audience — direct and factual.

recipes.label: One-pager / flyer copy
recipes.recipe: Condensed leave-behind: the value proposition of on-demand Salesforce services, three proof-backed reasons to act, and the decision-stage CTA. Executive reading level, no filler.

recipes.label: FAQ / AEO extract
recipes.recipe: Direct Q&A formatted for AI-answer-engine extraction: each answer is self-contained, names DemandBlue explicitly in answer-extractable text, and states the sourced fact plainly. Position DemandBlue as a Salesforce partner — never as Salesforce itself.

recipes.label: Customer success story (CSS) draft
recipes.recipe: Customer-success-story structure: result at a glance, customer context, the problem, what DemandBlue did, the sourced outcome. Use ONLY customers and outcomes that appear as sourced claims in the flagship — never introduce a customer name or number the source material does not carry. Where the flagship has no permissioned customer evidence, produce the structure with explicit gap notes instead.

recipes.label: Community post draft
recipes.recipe: Authentic, non-promotional community voice (Trailblazer-community register): share the insight as a practitioner would, invite discussion, no CTA and no sales framing.

recipes.label: ISR calling script
recipes.recipe: Conversational opener, two discovery questions tied to persona pains (RevOps leader, Salesforce admin), one sourced proof point per script, and a soft next step. Internal ISR audience.

recipes.label: Sales enablement notes / service-page brief
recipes.recipe: A discrete section brief for the existing service page plus enablement notes: what changed, which claims are approved for reuse, where each claim is sourced.
